text:
A king was walking in his garden when he met a little girl who was selling flowers.

“What do you have there?” asked the king.

“Flowers, Your Majesty,” said the girl. “They are one coin each.”

The king wanted to test her. “I will give you one coin,” he said, “but tell me: where does the sun go at night?”

“It goes to the same place where it was before, Your Majesty,” said the girl. “It is always shining somewhere.”

The king was surprised. “Very good! Now, tell me: how many stars are in the sky?”

“As many as the hairs on your head,” said the girl. “If you don’t believe me, you can count them.”

The king laughed loudly. “You are clever!” he said. “What do you want as a reward?”

The girl thought. “I don’t want gold,” she said. “I want to go to school. I want to learn many things.”

The king smiled. He sent her to the best school in the country. Many years later, she became a wise advisor to the king.

Moral: Knowledge is more valuable than gold.
